newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends down v dlr, RBI rolls over swaps.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends down v dlr, RBI rolls over swaps.

text.p: The Indian rupee fell sharply against the dollar on Wednesday because of sustained dollar buying by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and major purchases by a Calcutta-based state-run bank, dealers said.
The RBI bought spot dollars throughout the day, they said.
The Calcutta bank set the day's trend, bidding for dollars early in the morning, followed by the RBI, dealers said.
"They bought upto 35.81 level," said a dealer about the Calcutta bank. Dollar buying by the twosome created a flutter in the market. "There was some panic," said a dealer.

Dealers said RBI came in the forward swaps market in the evening to receive premia and sold dollars for May 1997 delivery. The RBI's earlier forward deals, close to $1.0 billion, are maturing this month, they said.
"Earlier they had said they would unwind their forward commitments," said a dealer, referring to RBI's roll over of forward deals in the swap market on Wednesday.
The RBI was not immediately available for comment.
"Maybe RBI wants to signal that they won't buy dollars (from the spot market) at any level," said a dealer. The RBI has been continuously buying spot dollars in recent months.
He said RBI was suggesting it would switch to swaps if the spot rate weakened. Another objective could be to push down the six month annualised forward premium to below 8.0 percent.
The six-month forward premium fell to 7.87 percent from 8.45 percent at close of trading, dealers said.
The spot dollar closed at 35.805/825 rupees, down from the opening level of 35.73/74, dealers said.
Some dealers said the spot dollar would weaken further later this month because of year-end dollar requirements of the central bank, state-run and private firms.
Export receivables, in contrast, are expected to be lower in December.
"Before the month-end it (dollar) will test 36 (rupees per dollar level) and then spring back," said Dayanand Nayak, chief foreign exchange dealer at Corporation Bank in Bombay.
Estimates of swap roll-overs RBI may resort to this month range from $200 million to $700 million.
"Today's swaps must be about $50 million - so you can expect more action in the days to come," said a dealer.
ICICI Securities and Finance Company said dollar purchases by the RBI in recent months exceeded $1.0 billion.
RBI's foreign currency assets rose to $19.53 billion on November 22 from $19.43 billion on November 15, the central bank said on Saturday.
